summary: 拓跋郁律子，质于后赵；即代王位，建元建国，都云中盛乐，始制法律、分土定居；屡北征高车、西击卫辰，代北强盛；建国三十九年为前秦所灭，北魏追尊昭成皇帝。
summary_en: Son of Tuoba Yulü, hostage in Later Zhao in his youth; taking the throne as King of Dai, he opened the era Jianguo with his capital at Shengle in Yunzhong, first made laws, and moved toward settled lands; campaigning north against the Gaoche and west against Weichen, the Dai realm grew strong in the north. In the 39th year of Jianguo Former Qin destroyed it; Northern Wei later honored him as Emperor Zhaocheng.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现北方草原之主的雄浑之态，衣冠从拓跋部制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 拓跋郁律子。幼质于后赵。
timeline.summary_en: Son of Tuoba Yulü; in childhood a hostage in Later Zhao.

timeline.title: 即代王位
timeline.summary: 即代王位，建元建国，都云中盛乐。
timeline.summary_en: He took the throne as King of Dai, opened the era Jianguo, and made Shengle in Yunzhong his capital.

timeline.title: 定法律
timeline.summary: 始制法律，分土定居倾向加强。
timeline.summary_en: He first fixed the laws, and the turn toward settled lands strengthened.

timeline.title: 破高车等
timeline.summary: 多次北征高车、西击卫辰等。
timeline.summary_en: He campaigned north again and again against the Gaoche and west against Weichen.

timeline.title: 前秦灭代
timeline.summary: 苻坚遣军灭代，什翼犍死，部众离散。
timeline.summary_en: Fu Jian's army destroyed Dai; Shiyijian died — the records differ on how — and his people scattered.

timeline.title: 昭成总评
timeline.summary: 北魏追尊昭成皇帝；为道武帝复国张本。
timeline.summary_en: Northern Wei honored him as Emperor Zhaocheng; he prepared the ground for Emperor Daowu's restoration.

bio_md:
# 代王 · 主要事迹

拓跋什翼犍，拓跋鲜卑首领，拓跋郁律之子。幼年质于后赵，见识中原制度。建国元年，什翼犍即代王位，建元建国，都云中盛乐——代国自此有年号、有都城，渐脱部落之习。

什翼犍之治，为拓跋部由部落联盟向国家过渡之关键：始制法律，「法令明整」；分土定居，「分筑城郭」；又置百官，仿晋制。军事上，屡北征高车、西击刘卫辰，代北强盛。建国三十九年，前秦苻坚遣军大举来攻，代国诸部溃散，什翼犍为其庶子寔君所杀（一说为苻坚所害），代国亡。

代国虽亡，然拓跋之根未绝：什翼犍之孙拓跋珪，于淝水之战后复国，改称魏，是为北魏道武帝。北魏追尊什翼犍为昭成皇帝。史家论什翼犍：立法建国，开北魏之先河——五胡诸国多旋兴旋亡，而拓跋氏历亡而不绝，终统一北方，其奠基之功，实自什翼犍始。

> 参考：点校本《魏书》卷1《序纪》、卷113《官氏志》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tuoba Shiyijian was a chief of the Tuoba Xianbei, son of Tuoba Yulü. In his youth he was a hostage in Later Zhao and saw the institutions of the Central Plains. In the 1st year of Jianguo he took the throne as King of Dai, opened the era Jianguo, and made Shengle in Yunzhong his capital — the Dai realm now had its own era and capital, and began to leave the tribal way behind.

His reign marks the passage of the Tuoba from tribal league to state: he first fixed the laws, "clear and strict"; he allotted the lands for settlement and "built walled towns"; he installed his officials on the Jin model. In arms he campaigned north again and again against the Gaoche and west against Liu Weichen, and the north grew strong under him. In the 39th year of Jianguo, Fu Jian of Former Qin came against him in force; the tribes scattered, and Shiyijian was slain by his own son Shijun (or, some say, by Fu Jian's men) — the Dai realm was no more.

But the Tuoba root was not cut: his grandson Tuoba Gui, after the Fei River defeat, restored the state under the name Wei — Emperor Daowu of Northern Wei. Northern Wei honored Shiyijian as Emperor Zhaocheng. The historians see in him the maker of the laws and statehood of the Tuoba, the forerunner of Northern Wei: of all the barbarian states, only the Tuoba fell and rose again to unite the north — and the foundation was laid by Shiyijian.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 1 ("Prefatory Annals"), ch. 113 (treatise on official clans).
